root_cause.text: WoW (Wake-on-Wireless) offloads were being applied to all virtual interface links in multi-link operation (MLO), but the WCN7850 firmware only supports these offloads on the primary link, causing a firmware crash when offloads were configured on secondary links.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds identical checks across five functions (`ath12k_wow_cleanup`, `ath12k_wow_set_wakeups`, `ath12k_wow_nlo_cleanup`, `ath12k_wow_arp_ns_offload`, and `ath12k_gtk_rekey_offload`) that skip processing for non-primary links using `if (arvif != &arvif->ahvif->deflink) continue;`. The CVE description explicitly states "WCN7850 firmware crashes due to WoW offloads enabled on both primary and secondary links" and the fix restricts offload configuration to "only on primary link." The regression was introduced by commit 32f7b19668bd which added MLO support without accounting for this firmware limitation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip WoW cleanup for non-default link virtual interfaces to prevent incorrect cleanup operations on secondary link interfaces.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check that skips processing if `arvif` is not equal to `&arvif->ahvif->deflink`, inserting a continue statement to move to the next list iteration before calling `ath12k_wow_vif_cleanup()`.
intent_record.how: This change filters the list iteration to only process virtual interfaces that are the default link of their associated hardware virtual interface. Virtual interfaces that are not the default link are skipped, preventing `ath12k_wow_vif_cleanup()` from being called on non-default link interfaces during WoW (Wake-on-Wireless) cleanup operations.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement appears in multiple WoW (Wake-on-Wireless) offload processing contexts (lines 137 and surrounding areas) where it iterates over all virtual interface entries without filtering for default links only. In multi-link operation (MLO), this causes WoW offloads (ARP/NS offload, GTK rekey, NLO cleanup, and wakeup configuration) to be incorrectly applied to secondary link interfaces, which the WCN7850 firmware does not support, resulting in firmware crashes. The vulnerability requires adding a guard check to process only the default link of each virtual interface.

bic_trace_step.reason: The code applies WoW offloads to ALL virtual interfaces without checking if they are on the primary link. In `ath12k_wow_set_wakeups()` (line 340-352), the function iterates through `list_for_each_entry(arvif, &ar->arvifs, list)` and calls `ath12k_vif_wow_set_wakeups(arvif, wowlan)` for every interface. Similarly, `ath12k_wow_cleanup()` (line 115-128) applies cleanup to all interfaces via `list_for_each_entry(arvif, &ar->arvifs, list)`. The vulnerability root cause states that WCN7850 firmware only supports WoW offloads on the primary link, but this code unconditionally configures offloads on all virtual interface links in MLO scenarios. There is no check for primary link status (e.g., `arvif->is_primary_link` or similar) before applying the offloads, which would cause firmware crashes when secondary links receive these configurations.
